phases.title: Prerequisites
phases.goal: The smallest set that makes trees, graphs and DP tractable: hashing, sorting, recursion, and the array patterns DP is built on.

phases.title: Trees & BST
phases.goal: Binary trees and BSTs. Traversals, the bottom-up pattern, tree DP, and the BST invariant.

phases.title: Graphs
phases.goal: Traversal, topological order, shortest paths, disjoint sets and minimum spanning trees.

phases.title: Dynamic Programming
phases.goal: Every DP family that appears in interviews: 1D, grids, knapsack, subsequences, strings, stocks, LIS and interval partition.

phases.title: Core Patterns
phases.goal: The remaining high-yield patterns across arrays, binary search, strings, linked lists, stacks, windows, heaps, greedy and bits.

phases.title: Advanced & Revision
phases.goal: Tries, the hardest leftovers, and the revision queue.

tiers.CORE: Code it fully. No shortcuts, no editorial. The pattern lives here.
tiers.DRILL: A variation on a CORE you already did. Under 10 minutes. If it takes 30, the CORE did not land.
tiers.SKIM: Read the learnings dropdown, write 3 lines of pseudocode, move on. Code it only if the day ran short.

revision.note: the Striver star - flag anything you want resurfaced

confidence.note: rate after solving. 1 = needed the editorial, 5 = could teach it

goodnotes_ref.note: free-text pointer to the GoodNotes page (e.g. 'DSA nb2 p.41'). Opaque to the system - never parsed.

my_approach.note: optional one-liner typed into the tracker on how he solved it. If it differs from the optimal, that gap is the revision signal.

revision_queue_rule: ORDER BY confidence ASC NULLS LAST, last_revised ASC NULLS FIRST WHERE status != 'todo' AND (revision = true OR confidence <= 3)

stuck_ladder.do: Brute force on paper, not the keyboard. Write the dumbest correct solution. Most 'stuck' is a skipped brute force.
Read the constraints. n tells you the target complexity: n<=20 bitmask or backtracking, n<=500 O(n^3), n<=5000 O(n^2), n<=1e5 O(n log n), n<=1e9 O(log n) or math.
Open the learnings dropdown. Read ONLY the insight line. Close it. Try again.
Read the trick line. Try again.
Striver video or TUF article, both linked inline. Then close every tab and reimplement from an empty file.

ai_protocol: Never before the 20 minute mark. The struggle is what encodes it.
Never paste the problem and ask for a solution.
Ask: 'Here is my approach: X. Where does it break?'
Ask: 'What invariant should I be maintaining here?'
Ask: 'I have an O(n^2). What property of the input am I not exploiting?'
After solving: 'Here is my code, review it like a FAANG interviewer.' Most valuable, least used.
Separate session, always. Keeps you from asking earlier and earlier.
Anything that needed a hint is not done, it is scheduled. Set confidence <= 3 and redo it cold in 48 hrs.

theory_parts.heading: Part 1 — The topic, in breadth
theory_parts.brief: What the topic is, how it works, how to implement it, what it costs. The answer you would get if you simply asked 'what is X'. Textbook register.

theory_parts.heading: Part 2 — Interview depth
theory_parts.brief: The deeper technical layer: only what gets probed in a technical round or as a follow-up. Trade-offs, worst cases, proofs, the grilling chain. Textbook register, heavier.

theory_parts.heading: Part 3 — If something above did not land
theory_parts.brief: A short, plain real-world analogy for the hard ideas in Parts 1 and 2. Warm, brief, and strictly a fallback.

closed_topic_rollup: Once a topic is finished, every learning in it is carried forward as a single consolidated line for the rest of the sheet. Arrays never vanishes - by the time you reach DP it is one dense paragraph instead of forty lines.
note_tiers: v2: every problem is CORE. The tier field remains for schema compatibility; hide it in the UI.

optional_appendix.note: Narrow one-off tricks. Not scheduled, not counted, not shown in the day view. Import into a separate optional list if you want them browsable.
